questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why placebos should replace active drugs in routine treatment of chronic disease
How the pharmaceutical industry developed and marketed sugar pills since the 1700s
How sham surgery became the standard method for testing new cancer treatments
How placebos work in trials, what effects they have, and what influences them
questions.explain: It defines placebos and discusses their effects, influencing factors, and depression research.

questions.q: What did the 2001 meta-analysis of 40 conditions find?
options: Nausea was the only effect
Placebos worked for most conditions
Placebos cured diseases
Only pain showed a significant effect
questions.explain: It concluded the only condition with a significant placebo effect was pain.

questions.q: Which delivery form is said to have the strongest placebo effect?
options: Injections
Capsules
Powders
Pills
questions.explain: Capsules appear more influential than pills, and injections are even stronger than capsules.

questions.q: In the open/hidden studies, when were analgesics more effective?
options: When they were given secretly without the patient being told
When the patient knew they were receiving them
When they were combined with a placebo in a blinded trial
When they were given by a doctor the patient had never met
questions.explain: Analgesics are considerably more effective when the patient knows they are receiving them.

questions.q: Why is a no-treatment comparison group not enough to prove a true placebo effect?
options: Placebo groups are too small to produce reliable results
It is not blinded, so bias could create differences
Regression to the mean cannot be ruled out in such groups
Patients in it tend to drop out before the study ends
questions.explain: The authors note lack of blinding could produce differences between placebo and no-treatment groups even without a true effect.
